title: Microscopy at REVA
question: What is visible at one scale that disappears at another?
summary: This proposed study pairs a microscope image with a magnified detail. The preview uses a synthetic field to demonstrate one way to examine an ambiguous boundary.

provenance.scope: Research context and proposed comparison. The lab image and methods are pending.

figure.alt: An abstract field of oval forms with a box around an area for closer inspection.
figure.caption: A synthetic field marks an area for closer inspection.
figure.source: Original CSS diagram created for this portfolio preview.

scene.alt: Oval forms are distributed across a synthetic field. A square marks a cluster near the center.
scene.caption: The box locates the area shown in the magnified detail.
scene.source: Original CSS diagram created for this portfolio preview.

detail.alt: The same boxed area is enlarged, showing two oval outlines meeting near the middle.
detail.caption: The marked area is shown at twice the display size. Two outlines meet near the center.
detail.source: Original CSS diagram created for this portfolio preview.

decision.title: Keep the area of uncertainty in view
decision.description: The box shows exactly where the close-up came from. In the close-up, the outlines are easier to follow, but their meeting point still admits two readings: one continuous boundary or two overlapping edges. The pair gives a reader a location to revisit before tracing a contour.

caseStudy.limitation: Both panels use the same synthetic field. The study still needs a cleared image and annotation, documented methods, and an example of ambiguity drawn from the actual material.
